newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan foreign minister to fly to Peru.
newsitem.headline: Japan foreign minister to fly to Peru.

text.p: Japanese Foreign Minister Yukihiko Ikeda said on Wednesday he would fly to Peru to help resolve a hostage crisis at the Japanese ambassador's residence in Lima.
"I will go to Peru tomorrow (Thursday) after discussions with Prime Minister (Ryutaro) Hashimoto," he told a news conference.
Ikeda said there had been no contact with Japanese ambassador to Peru Morihisa Aoki, who is among some 200 hostages being held by leftist guerrillas at his residence, since his last call at 0930 GMT.
"We have had no contact with Ambassador (Morihisa) Aoki since the last call (at 0930 GMT)," Ikeda said.
The guerrillas from the Tupac Amaru Revolutionary Movement (MRTA) demanded contact with President Alberto Fujimori within 20 minutes.
In a previous television interview a little before midday, the rebels said there had been no communication with Peruvian authorities.

The rebels stormed the residence Tuesday night during a reception attended by several senior diplomats and government ministers. They are demanding the release of up to 500 comrades held in Peruvian jails.
Earlier on Wednesday a loud explosion and gunfire were heard from inside the residence. It was not known if anyone was injured.
